gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the SwitchBot kit's 4.3-inch monitor is 480×272 pixels (130,560 px), 7.8 times fewer pixels than the eufy Smart Display E10's 8-inch 1280×800 screen (1,024,000 px). The monitor can show only about 4% of the doorbell's own 2304×1296 '2K' frame.
standout_why: I read the cited Smart Home Perfected page and the top results from WorthRated, drunvalo.net and indoorsecuritycamera.com. All of them give the monitor's size in inches and the camera's resolution ('2K', '1080P'). None gives the monitor's own pixel count for any product. SwitchBot's 480×272 and the E10's 1280×800 appear on none of them. Smart Home Perfected lists the SwitchBot's 165° and 5000 mAh but not the screen resolution, and it gives no battery-life basis for any product. Drunvalo says it measured about 6 hours unplugged for the E10, but it does not put screen resolutions side by side.
decides: This confirms eufy E340 + E10 as the pick when the indoor screen is the reason to buy: 8-inch 1280×800 screen, and a live feed that comes up on its own when the bell rings. SwitchBot ($149.99 with monitor) becomes the budget pick with a stated catch: its 2K camera is shown on a 480×272 screen. PCWorld also found you must press play and wait several seconds when the bell rings. So '2K' on the doorbell says nothing about what you see on the monitor.

findings.label: On-device storage and the basis of the days claim
findings.value: 8 GB; '90 days' based on 30 clips × 20 s per day (10 min/day, so about 15 h of video in total)

findings.note: Footnote: 'based on an average of recording 30 videos, each of 20 seconds in length, per day.' 90 × 30 × 20 s = 54,000 s = 15 h. The page also lists a 160° viewing angle without saying which axis, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only, and $169.99 for the doorbell alone.

findings.label: Kit price, SwitchBot US store
findings.note: Read with storecheck.py search. The description mentions 'the monitor's WiFi relay' and says it 'works even without internet'.

findings.label: Battery-life claim basis
findings.value: 5000 mAh; the maker states only '*Tested under SwitchBot Lab conditions. Actual performance may vary'. It gives no triggers per day.
findings.note: PCWorld quotes the claim as 'up to 19 months'. The E340 page gives no battery-life figure at all, so the two batteries cannot be compared on a common basis.

findings.label: Monitor resolution vs camera resolution
findings.value: Monitor 4.3 in, 480 × 272 px (130,560 px; about 128 ppi). Camera 2304 × 1296 px (2,985,984 px). The monitor shows 4.4% of the camera's pixels.
findings.source_title: SwitchBot Smart Video Doorbell review: monitor included (PCWorld, Christopher Null, 2025-11-10)
findings.note: Christopher Null lists 'Display has very low resolution' as a con. My arithmetic: 130,560 ÷ 2,985,984 = 4.4%. The E10 has 1,024,000 ÷ 130,560 = 7.8 times the pixels. Diagonal √(480²+272²) = 552 px ÷ 4.3 in = 128 ppi.

findings.label: Monitor power and ring behaviour
findings.value: Wall plug only (two-prong). Video does not appear automatically on ring: you press play and wait several seconds.
findings.source_title: SwitchBot Smart Video Doorbell review: monitor included (PCWorld)
findings.note: PCWorld also gives the doorbell-to-monitor range as 100 m in open air, with SwitchBot recommending 5–10 m in practice. The doorbell can trickle-charge from a 24 V doorbell transformer.
